description: A homeowner with one spare bedroom must decide whether to accept a prospective subletter's informal arrangement and finalize the rent, occupancy dates, household help, guest limit, and trust checks with the people gathered at the house.

agents.name: Ravi
agents.role: Mina's Friend Who Knows the Fallback Applicant

shared_context.S1: Mina has one furnished bedroom available in her house.
shared_context.S2: The room is currently being discussed for a late-summer-to-winter sublet.
shared_context.S3: Mina makes the final call on whether to accept an arrangement and what terms to agree.
shared_context.S4: The house has one shared dog, and the current household has been looking for a reliable way to cover its daily walks.

PF1.text: Jordan is prepared to pay exactly $725 per month, occupy the room from September 1 through December 31, and handle exactly three dog-walking shifts each week in exchange for that arrangement, but has not yet stated those terms to Mina.

PF2.text: Tess checked the lease with the landlord and learned that overnight guests may stay no more than exactly two nights per month; Tess also spoke with Jordan's former landlord, who confirmed that Jordan paid on time throughout the prior tenancy, and neither point has been shared with Mina.

PF3.text: Ravi knows that a fallback applicant is ready to take the same room for exactly $700 per month if Mina does not reach an agreement with Jordan; Ravi learned this directly from that applicant and has not told Mina yet.

acceptance_conditions: Mina must accept Jordan as the subletter.
The monthly rent must be exactly $725.
The occupancy must run from September 1 through December 31.
Jordan must commit to exactly three dog-walking shifts per week.
The guest limit must be exactly two overnight guest nights per month.
Jordan's former-landlord reference must be explicitly confirmed.
The fallback applicant's alternative rent must be recorded as exactly $700 per month.
The settlement must include commitments for the dog-walking arrangement and the guest limit.

content_checks.C5: decisions['dog_walking_shifts_per_week'] == 3 and any(c['type'] == 'dog_walking' or c['type'] == 'dog_walking_shifts' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['guest_nights_per_month'] == 2 and any(c['type'] == 'guest_policy' or c['type'] == 'guest_limit' or c['type'] == 'lease_compliance' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jordan's undisclosed proposal changes the subletter to Jordan, the rent to exactly $725, the dates to September 1 through December 31, and the household contribution to exactly three dog-walking shifts per week.

Tess's lease and reference information changes the guest limit to exactly two overnight nights per month and changes the trust check from unconfirmed to a confirmed former-landlord reference that Mina must credit to Tess.
Ravi's fallback-applicant information changes the recorded alternative from unknown to exactly $700 per month, giving Mina the concrete comparison for Jordan's $725 arrangement.
